findings.title: Finite need, bounded means, taught knowledge
findings.claim: The instructed entry can complete a finite need held within Jacob while remaining unable to control the event sequence, and the knowledge attributed to Jacob includes recognizing that limit of means.
findings.mechanism: The focus carries the act through the ordered entry and the negated availing construction, then locates the exception in Jacob's inner need and marks that need as completed. Wider supplied relations connect this act to divine judgment, reliance, the failure of protectors, and knowledge received by teaching; those contacts return through the focus forms for need, inner self, availing, completion, and knowledge, changing the reading from a single protective tactic into a distinction between inward completion and outward control.
findings.reader_payoff: Planning and knowledge can now be seen together without making precaution sovereign: the means has a real human purpose, while the result remains outside its power.
findings.containment: The finding preserves the plain account of the brothers entering by their father's instruction. It does not identify the exact exposure Jacob feared, make the plan pointless, grant Jacob unrestricted knowledge, or treat any wider parallel as a verdict on every detail of the scene.

epistemic.reason: The trusted cross-run publication maps all five branches to exact focus carriers; the reader-walk supports and wider connections are legacy-unbound or nomination evidence, so their corroborating force is retained with explicit qualification.

branch_activations.facet_statement: Temel durum, bir şey olmadan yapamama ve ona gereksinim duymadır.
branch_activations.carrier: The indefinite حاجةً names the bounded need or concern for which the entry is undertaken.

branch_activations.activation: That action-and-reliance frame meets حاجةً as the finite concern held inside Jacob, making the exception readable as inward need fulfillment while the act remains under reliance.
branch_activations.resulting_reading: Prudence has a real, bounded object: it can settle a need without guaranteeing the brothers' safety or the route of events.
branch_activations.boundary: The exact exposure and the single motive behind Jacob's need remain open; the branch is retained at its core need facet only.

branch_activations.boundary: This does not decide whether the inner content is procedure, memory, or affective relief, and it does not turn the inner self into a separate lexical gloss.

findings.title: Knowledge beside bounded hope
findings.claim: The later father's hope in 12:83 lets the focus's taught knowledge remain alongside a human hope for reunion, so knowledge can guide hope without becoming control of the route.
findings.mechanism: The supplied reciprocal connection and retrospective support return from 12:83 to the focus assertion of knowledge through 12:68:23:1. The later scene places limited agency beside divine knowledge, making the focus's separation between a real inward completion and an uncontrolled outward course visible as a continuing relation.
findings.reader_payoff: The focus's knowledge clause becomes more precise: it supports informed hope and judgment while leaving the path and outcome open.
findings.containment: This is a retrospective echo, not a claim that 12:83 identifies Jacob's exact need in 12:68 or that the later scene supplies a focus-level lexical branch. The reciprocal source is a nomination requiring fresh assessment, and target morphology is not supplied.

epistemic.reason: The evidence is a legacy-unbound retrospective walk and a reciprocal nomination, with exact 12:83 Arabic supplied but no target morphology; the relation is retained as qualified contextual evidence.

findings.title: A later opening beyond the precaution
